title: C528/303/2024 of HARISH KUNIYAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
23.08.2024 C-482 Petition No. 299 of 2024
With
C528 Petition No. 303 of 2024
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Ms. Sudha Tamta, learned counsel
for the applicant.
2. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, Brief Holder
for the State.
3. The issue involved in both these
applications pertains to a complaint
preferred by the present applicant under
Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments
Act, 1881. Two separate Complaints
under Section 138 of the NI Act were filed
against the respondent no.2 and after
concluding the proceeding of the
Complaints under Section 138 of the NI
Act, the respondent no.2 was convicted
vide order dated 26th March, 2022 passed
by 1st Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun.
Against which, two separate Criminal
Appeals i.e. Criminal Appeal No. 67 of
2022 and Criminal Appeal No. 68 of 2022
were preferred, in which, the respondent-complainant was enlarged on bail and the
order convicting the respondent dated
26.03.2022 was also suspended and the
appellant /respondent no. 2 was directed
to deposit 20% of the amount of
compensation in view of Section 148 of
the N.I. Act within 60 days. It is
submitted that after being released on
bail, the respondent no. 2 never turned
up to appear before the Appellate Court
nor he has complied with the conditions
as stipulated in the order dated 25th April,

2022.
4. It is submitted by learned counsel
for the applicant that when the condition
as stipulated in the order was not
complied with then non-bailable warrants
were issued and for recalling of the same
an application was moved and NBW was
recalled on 12.04.2024. Despite this,
neither the respondent no.2 has complied
with the condition by depositing 20% of
the amount of compensation nor is he
putting appearance in the Criminal
Appeal.
5. Now, by the instant application, the
present applicant is praying for
expeditious disposal of both the criminal
appeals, i.e., Criminal Appeal No. 67 of
2022 and Criminal Appeal No. 68 of 2022,
pending in the court District and Sessions
Jude, Dehradun.
6. Admittedly, as per the order dated
12.04.2024 it appears that the
respondent no. 2 has not complied with
the conditions as stipulated in the order
dated 25.04.2022 and, this itself shows
that respondent no. 2 is adopting the
delaying tactics which is deliberate on his
part. The complaint under Section 138 of
the NI Act was filed in the year 2018 and
the same was concluded and decided by
the Judicial Magistrate on 26.03.2022.
7. As per the mandate of Section
143(3) of the NI Act, the complaint
preferred under Section 138 of the NI Act
should be decided within six months and
though the proceedings of the complaint
has already been concluded and the two
separate Criminal Appeals have been
preferred by the respondent no.2 but the
respondent is adopting the delaying
tactics. The Appellate Court, lastly

passed the order on 12th April, 2024 and
granted one more opportunity to the
respondent/complainant to fulfil the
condition as per Section 148 in
compliance to the order dated 25.04.2022
but uptill the same has yet not been
complied with. It appears that the
respondent is adopting deliberately a
delaying tactics, therefore, in such an
eventuality, the Appellate Court is
directed to decide the Criminal Appeals as
early as possible preferably within two
months from the date of presentation of
certified copy of this Order.
8. Subject to the observations as
above, both the C528 Applications, (C528
Petition No. 299 of 2024 and C528
Petition No. 303 of 2024), are disposed of.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 23.08.2024
Kaushal
